In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in the development of obesity and the related comorbidities.
the study of the role of CART and its gene polymorphisms in the regulation of energy balance, body composition and bone metabolism.
the development of a new class of drugs for the treatment of osteoporosis and related disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CART promoter SNP- 3608 C allele, which confers resistance to obesity, is also protective against low BMD, which is a major risk factor for osteoporosis and fracture.
the CART gene polymorphism is associated with BMD at non-weight bearing sites in humans, and that the CART gene may play a role in bone remodeling in post-menopausal women.
obesity susceptibility CART gene polymorphisms contribute to bone remodeling in humans, which is in line with the recently established role of the CART gene in bone remodeling in mice [1].

CART is a key player in the regulation of both body weight and BMD.
